name: Olala-v1.0-mini-7A1B
family: Olala (hybrid Mamba-3 + differential attention, latent MoE)
context_scaling: Card prints 'Context length 32K tokens (input + output)' and says a 128K version is coming soon; config.json declares max_position_embeddings 100000 with sliding_window_size 65536, so the config allows more than the vendor-supported limit. The recorded value is the card's supported 32K.
attention_variant: Hybrid: 29 Mamba-3 layers (d_state 128, headdim 64, MIMO dim 4, gated delta-style update) + 7 differential-attention layers with MLA-compressed KV (mla_kv_rank 128, num_attention_heads 48, head_dim 128, num_key_value_heads 0 i.e. no separate K/V heads), one attention layer in five; every layer followed by a latent MoE block (256 routed / 6 active + 1 shared).
notes: ADDED 2026-11-22 by the trending sweep. First European sovereign-lab model in this catalog and the best fit yet for the low-VRAM + large-RAM box: 6.8B total parameters but only about 1B active per token, and only 7 of 36 layers keep anything that grows with context, so 29/36 layers can sit in system RAM with no cache penalty. PARAMS: HF API safetensors.total 6,773,124,144 (6,756,461,568 BF16 + 16,662,576 F32 header tensors), matching the card's '6.8B total, about 1B active per token'. The active figure is a VENDOR claim, not derived here; a shape check supports it - per MoE layer the 6 routed experts cost 3 x 384 x 768 x 6 = 5.3M weights and the shared expert 3 x 1536 x 1536 = 7.1M, so 36 x ~12.5M = ~450M of the active path is experts, with the rest in the Mamba-3 mixers and the 7 attention layers. KV BASIS: 1792 bytes/token = 7 attention layers x mla_kv_rank 128 x 2 bytes. This counts only the MLA latent; any per-layer RoPE key component is NOT included because the config does not print its dimension (rope_theta is 0.0 and rope_type is empty, both inherited from the MLA block), so treat 1792 as a floor. The 29 Mamba-3 layers hold a constant recurrent state instead of a cache: with hidden 1536 / mamba_headdim 64 = 24 heads, the per-layer state is 24 x 64 x d_state 128 = 196,608 elements, i.e. ~22.8 MB per sequence across 29 layers at fp32 - constant in context length but not small, and it is per concurrent sequence, not per token. That arithmetic is DERIVED from config keys (mamba_d_state, mamba_headdim, hidden_size, num layers), not printed by the vendor, and the state dtype could be bf16 which would halve it. WHY IT IS A RECORD: the card prints a 19-model, 13-benchmark table and this model is the strongest of the 7-8B-class MoE entries on 9 of the 13 rows against its closest comparator LFM2.5 8B-A1B (IFBench 57.7 vs 48.3, LIFEBench 79.3 vs 77.8, DROP 83.8 vs 73.1, GPQA Diamond 50.5 vs 41.9, HumanEval+ 88.3 vs 79.9, MBPP+ 75.1 vs 64.2, AIME 2025 61.3 vs 48.0, AIME 2026 52.7 vs 48.0, MGSM 68.7 vs 60.5), ties Multi-IF (71.2 vs 71.0) and LOSES TruthfulQA (66.6 vs 68.9), AIME 2024 (60.7 vs 64.7) and BFCL V3 (59.6 vs 69.7). It also beats Qwen3.5-2B dense on IFBench 57.7 vs 35.3 and HumanEval+ 88.3 vs 48.3 at similar active cost. LOSES THAT MATTER: it is not competitive with 3-4B dense reasoners - Qwen3.5-4B takes GPQA (75.8 vs 50.5), AIME 2024 (80.7 vs 60.7), AIME 2025 (74.7 vs 61.3), MGSM (88.8 vs 68.7) and DROP (86.3 vs 83.8), and LFM3-1.7B - a 1.7B model - takes IFBench 70.0 vs 57.7. The card says so itself: 'strongest on instruction following and weakest on competition mathematics', 68.0 twelve-benchmark average and +15.2 over its own SFT checkpoint. RELATION: base_model is the family's SFT checkpoint (card tag base_model Olala-v1.0-mini-7A1B-SFT, relation finetune); neither the -base nor the -SFT repo is a catalog record, so this entry is not measured against a catalog-tracked parent, and the +15.2 is the card's own SFT-vs-post-trained delta. Same config.json as the SFT checkpoint (6.77B, 36 layers, 256/6 experts). Apache 2.0 with published training emissions (40 kt CO2eq, 1.16 GWh, JUPITER GH200 x 1,024) - the first model here with a disclosed pre-training energy figure. GAPS: no GGUF, MLX or other quant was seen on the Hub at sweep time, and 6.8B bf16 is ~13.6 GB, so it fits a 16 GB card or the 19 GiB Vulkan box unquantized but not with much context.

benchmarks.name: IFBench
benchmarks.config: Card 'Benchmarks' HTML table, column 'Olala v1.0-mini-7A1B 7B-A1B'. Beats its same-class comparator LFM2.5 8B-A1B 48.3, Qwen3.5-2B 35.3, Qwen3.5-4B 49.7, Granite 4.0-H-Tiny 44.5; LOSES to LFM3-1.7B at 70.0 and LFM2.5 2.6B at 59.0, and only ties Ling 3.0-tiny 57.3. Vendor numbers, no seed or interval.

benchmarks.name: Multi-IF
benchmarks.config: Same table. LFM2.5 8B-A1B 71.0 (a 0.2-point win, i.e. a tie within noise), Granite 4.0-H-Tiny 44.5; loses to Ling 3.0-tiny 75.2, Qwen3.5-4B 71.8 and LFM3-1.7B 83.6.

benchmarks.name: LIFEBench
benchmarks.config: Same table, long-instruction following. LFM2.5 8B-A1B 77.8, Qwen3.5-2B 82.0 (loss), Qwen3.5-4B 84.0 (loss), Ling 3.0-tiny 82.3 (loss).

benchmarks.name: GPQA Diamond
benchmarks.config: Same table. LFM2.5 8B-A1B 41.9, Qwen3.5-2B 63.1, Qwen3.5-4B 75.8, Ling 3.0-tiny 68.7 - the model is far behind 2-4B dense models on knowledge. Recorded as printed; this is the row that keeps the record out of the top of its class.

benchmarks.name: DROP
benchmarks.config: Same table. LFM2.5 8B-A1B 73.1, Qwen3.5-2B 81.4; loses Qwen3.5-4B 86.3 and Olmo 3-7B-Think 86.7.

benchmarks.name: HumanEval+
benchmarks.config: Same table. LFM2.5 8B-A1B 79.9, Qwen3.5-4B 83.4, Qwen3.5-2B 48.3, Granite 4.0-H-Tiny 77.4; loses Falcon H1R-7B 93.4 and Ministral 3-8B-Reasoning 93.8.

benchmarks.name: AIME 2025
benchmarks.config: Same table. LFM2.5 8B-A1B 48.0, Ling 3.0-tiny 70.0 (loss), Qwen3.5-4B 74.7 (loss), Falcon H1R-7B 82.7 (loss). Competition maths is the model's stated weak point.

benchmarks.name: MGSM
benchmarks.config: Same table, multilingual maths. LFM2.5 8B-A1B 60.5, Granite 4.0-H-Tiny 62.0; loses Qwen3.5-4B 88.8, Qwen3.5-2B 73.3 and LFM2.5 2.6B 75.7.

benchmarks.name: BFCL V3
benchmarks.config: Same table, tool use. LOSES to LFM2.5 8B-A1B 69.7, Ling 3.0-tiny 68.3, Qwen3.5-4B 67.8 and Falcon H1R-7B 67.8; beats Granite 4.0-H-Tiny 60.2 only marginally. The card's tool-calling training claim is not supported by this row.

benchmarks.name: Twelve-benchmark average
benchmarks.config: Card prose: 'Over twelve benchmarks, Olala-v1.0-mini-7A1B averages 68.0, 15.2 points above its SFT checkpoint.' An aggregate the card prints, not a benchmark; the +15.2 is a comparison against its own Olala-v1.0-mini-7A1B-SFT checkpoint, which is not a catalog record.

benchmarks.name: BFCL v3
benchmarks.config: Zero-shot BFCL V3, all 23 categories (4,981 samples), reasoning_effort=high for Olala models (card default is medium but benchmark used high), temperature=0.8, top_p=0.9, top_k=40, inspect_ai + vLLM, 64K context/no separate answer-length limit, float32 Mamba state; accuracy, 1 sample.
